newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals - Higher import duty on semis favoured.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals - Higher import duty on semis favoured.

text.p: India's non-ferrous metals industry and trade have demanded a higher import duty on semi-finished products compared to raw materials to help domestic units, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said industrial users of non-ferrous metals were either importing or buying semi-finished products instead of raw materials which in turn affected the local producers.
"The duty differential between semi-finished products and raw materials should at least be 15 percent," said Bombay Metals Exchange (BME) president Sharad Parikh.
At present the total duty on imported raw material and semi-finished products is uniform at 51.80 percent, including excise and taxes.

Parikh said the BME had in a memorandum to the finance ministry also suggested streamlining excise rules and incorporating the changes in the national budget for 1997/98 (April/March), scheduled for presentation on February 28.

Dealers said the prices of Indian non-ferrous raw materials depended on those of the London Metals Exchange (LME). The local producers such as the Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) and the Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) adjust their prices to match those of imports.
On Tuesday HZL revised its price by 180 rupees per tonne following a rise in the prices of imported zinc.
"Nobody wants to buy raw materials from the local units, the cost of which is on a par with imported raw material or semi-finished material," Parikh said.
In the week to Wednesday, copper gained 100 rupees to 12,600 rupees per quintal (100 kgs) and zinc 200 rupees to 6,750 rupees per quintal. Lead gained 100 rupees to 4,550 rupees per quintal.
Tin and nickel were losers, shedding 200 rupees and 400 rupees per quintal to 34,500 rupees and 36,500 rupees respectively.
Dealers said they expected the market to remain subdued in the next few weeks ahead of the budget, though local prices could keep pace with the trends on the LME.
